reviewText: This is a remaster with good sound quality.  Like all Gentle Giant albums, there have been several different CD releases of In A Glass House, with varying sound quality.  You need to be careful when buying a Gentle Giant CD to ensure you get good quality.The original album was 37 minutes.  This has an additional 20 minutes of bonus live material.There is a 30th Anniversary version of In A Glass House coming out soon.  It will be much cheaper than this CD.  I understand that it also has the bonus material, but I haven't been able to confirm that.This is album that Gentle Giant fans speak most fondly about.  I don't know why.  Maybe it is the nice cover that had a cel image of the band on top a another image of the band for a "3D" effect.  Or maybe it is because the LP was never released in the US, coming out just as the band was starting to gain some popularity (between Octopus and Power and Glory).  In spite of being available only as a costly import, it was the third biggest selling Gentle Giant LP in the US.  This album kind of got lost in the shuffle as Gentle Giant was moving from Columbia records to Capitol.  So, when more fans discovered Gentle Giant when Free Hand was released, those earlier collectors could amaze their friends by pulling out a copy of In A Glass House.The sound is much different than other Gentle Giant albums.  In A Glass House actually describes the music.  The album starts out with glass breaking.  The music on this entire album has that sharp, shattering sound.  Derek Shuman had left the group, so there is very little sax and no flute.  There is a lot of high ringing vibes and guitar work.Gentle Giant's live preformances during this period also had a starker, stripped down sound.  At some points in concert, they were much more like a convention rock band.In the next three ablums after this, Gentle Giant would return to the lusher, more mellow sound.

reviewText: "Cargo" came rapidly on the heels of "Business As Usual", due to, among other things, the amazing staying power and deserved popularity of that first album.As a complete piece, "Cargo" really can't compare, but it completely avoids the dreaded "sophomore slump" afflicting most new bands."Overkill" still stands a great single from the '80's, and there are a number of other equally engaging tracks on the disc, "No Restrictions", "High Wire", "It's A Mistake".But to be fair, there are other songs that are just a bit boring...made more so if you listen to their first two albums back to back.Here's the thing: you'll NEED this record if you buy the first one. They're sort of two pieces of a better whole. And there's enough here to make your purchase worthy.One last thing - I loved Colin Hay's voice. It was one of the better ones on the radio at the time...and you always knew immediately who it was...

reviewText: The 70's were unarguably the truest point in time for soul music. Motown got a big hit when Marvin Gaye put soul on a new plateau, mainly because he put his entire soul to this golden piece. Throughout his whole career, he tried to find a balance between spirituality and sexuality; on "What's Going On", he found spritual enlightenment in order to tell what has been going on with him, from his brother returning home, changed from the bloodshed of the Vietnam war (a senseless war that took so many innocent lives), living with the hostile realities of America's inner cities, the future of the planet, and his relationship with both his natural father and his spiritual father. This was Marvin Gaye's most monumental accomplishment and took soul music to new levels, and artists such as Curtis Mayfield took it further. Whether you are living good or barely living you should listen to this.

reviewText: Rhino has become synonymous with great, well remastered rejuvenation of classic artistes and their classic albums and most of the time, they get it right.  However, although the track selections are brilliant and with 20 tracks on one disc you are getting great value for money and great liner notes written by members of the band themselves, the usually brilliantly remastered sound quality that you'd expect from a Rhino album just isn't here on this album.  The sound quality is okay but not as good as most of their other projects.  Still, this is the one (pun intended)to get if you are looking for the best compilation of Orleans that is currently out there.  While they have been compared with other bands like Poco and Firefall, Player and Ambrosia, I'd say they rank behind Ambrosia in terms of quality but way ahead of the others mentioned.  Very good soft 70's style rock if you like that genre; if you like what you hear on this album, may I also recommend to you "Anthology" by Ambrosia which is one heck of a great album.

reviewText: BYTTB is fun, playful and different, just like on "Sisters of Avalon". I totally love "Into the Nightlife". What a fantastic song! Hopefully this will be Cyndi's 1st single. A perfect song for summer listening on your ipod. The chorus is catchy and the beat is bouncy and flowing. Totally a clubfloor smash hit. Tracks 1 & 2 pretty much run one into another like 1 long song. A perfect opener, although track 1 is a little less outstanding than track 2. Finally Cyndi has written new material. It's been too long since she came out with an album of all new stuff."Rocking Chair" totally depicts my love of rocking chairs. This is my theme song. lol Cyndi has a lot of fun with the vocal layering and ad lib in her fun Brooklyn accent. "Rocking Chair" is a very fun song indeed.The opening 2 minutes of "Echo" would remind you of a Kylie Minogue song in a way, because of the keyboards & beat. But then the song picks up in the chorus and totally blows the intro out of the water. Very summery and could work as a perfect clubfloor song too, in the hands of the right remixer/s."Lyfe" takes another turn, visiting Cyndi's bluesy style. A little R&B; mixed with some chillout, urban sound. So far, the CD is totally working with me, unlike any of Cyndi's other albums (upon first listen). That is good. "Lyfe" has nice vocal layering and it's a sexy song. Makes me think of something Kristine W has done on her "Land of the Living" album."Same Ol' Story" is a clubfloor dancehit without a doubt. Every aspect of this song makes it simply one of Cyndi's best songs to date. Even with the F word heard throughout the chorus, I just love the song. Like they say, good things come to this whom wait, and this album is a true gem, worth the wait."Raging Storm".......here we go again with another dancefloor hit. Nothing boring yet. The song style follows in the previous tracks footsteps."Lay Me Down" starts out slow and picks up with sort of a disco beat but not as fast-paced as the previous tracks. It's a little more alternative in a way, with the pop sound interlaced. Lyrically one of the best songs on the album, I think."Give It Up".......ok, back to the dancy stuff again. Honestly, I'm not sorry for buying the album or for hurrying out to the store to get it first thing in the morning, half-asleep. lol Once again, this song is interlaced with electronica, disco and a pure nightlife clubfloor hopping edge."Set Your Heart" starts out sounding exactly like Pet Shop Boys "Saturday Night" chorus line. Another true dancy number. So far, if you were dancing to the entire album, your legs would fall off. Another winner through and through, especially in the chorus line. So dancy and moving, I want to get up and dance to it as I write this."Grab A Hold" could've worked out well on Cyndi's first 2 CDs. Very cute, moving and dancy. Her voice is less mature here and that's why I'm reminded of her earlier cds. The chorus line is strong and powerful, rich with Cyndi's strong lungs and crystal clear vocals."Rain on Me" closes the album in a less dancy style but with catchy lyrics and a floating keyboard riff. Very 80's reminiscent but modern too. Cyndi's band sure knows how to arrange magic around Cyndi's voice. What a beautiful song.About the booklet & artwork:.....well, the cd is housed in a clear jewel case with front & back inserts and comes with a booklet full of fun pics of Cyndi. They are put through a hazy filter though, so it's got that dreamy effect. But the pics are still amusing, especially the one of her in the garden in her blue gown. The booklet is made of of a 2-sided, 3-fold layout with pics and credits. There aren't any lyrics. And inside the cd tray are Cyndi's Thank Yous'.Those are my thoughts on the album, for you all to read. I think you should go and get multiple copies of the cd for family & friends. It's a true winner and certainly worth the wait. The cd should be rated 10 stars.
summary: Diverse Dance & Pop Music at its Best!

reviewText: DMX's fourth album "The Great Depression" (2001), continues the saga of Yonkers MC Earl Simmons. Alot of rappers fall off, but X is still keeping it real and surviving and thriving three years after his first album. Album begins with "School Street" a shoutout/dedication track to fallen friends. Next comes "Who we Be" which uses a repetitive heavy bass beat, while X talks about his trials and tribulations. Next comes "Trina Moe", another banging track, where X talks about how alot of rappers talk about nothing important (cars,hoes,watches), and are not real with there people. The lead single "We Right Here" is another banging hiphop album which brings back the X we all know and love from past albums, dark and memorable. "Shorty was Da Bomb" continues X's pattern of dropping at least one track about the ladies, its entertaining,funny and X sings on it which surprisingly sounds good. "Damien III", has X facing Damien for the first time, and asking for the lords help for first time, another good track, kind of shows how X is progressing, love the way X sounds on this one. "When I'M Nothing" feat. Stephanine Mills, starts off real well, and X drops real nice verse on it, but Mills messes track up, with annoying vocal sound. "I Miss You" feat. Faith Evans is a powerfull track dedicated to X's grandmother, family, and religon. P. Killer produced "Ima Bang" is a blazing hot track, good track to bump in the ride. "Minute for your Son" closes off the album, with X thanking the lord, and all though it might not be the entertainment some want, it is a really positive track, and a rarity in hiphop, a track that is REALLY dedicated to God, X talks about being very happy for the first time in years. What I like about this album is DMX stays real, he doesnt just follow the same boring format some rappers do, never changing there styles, never taking the risk, and in the end just selling out to sell more, instead he changes up and stays real to himself, even if its not the commerical or pure hardcore album some want. End of last track is extended, and displays  artists from X's bloodline label. Not a classic album, because it does have some weaknesses, and at times is slow, but overall its another strong effort from one of Hiphops best.

reviewText: Here's the deal : you have to be a country music lover. Each of these songs separately is excellent; the first four songs alone are a mini-Knopfler CD of the highest quality, and could easily fit on Dire Straits albums, perhaps especially the rockabilly-tinged "On Every Street." On "This Is Us," the tempo is vintage Straits, Knopfler's elegant and melodious guitarwork is superb throughout the album, restrained and elegant yet as essential as a blistering solo from his rock heyday. After those first four songs, though... as I said: you have to love country music. Personally, I begin to not doze off but be so bored that I wish I could doze off.Harris seems to specialize in adding her Nashville cachet and golden pipes to ageing rockers these days, but she does much more for Knopfler than she did for Neil Young. Her voice is so different from Knopfler's that, although at first she seems to play second banana to his overwhelming presence, slowly you realize that she brings a whole new dimension to his mournful, somewhat monotonous voice. If I could digest a full hour of country without getting a rash, I would give this five stars. I can't, so here's three, hoping this assessment is helpful to those who feel the way I do.

reviewText: After 18 years in hiding, Odessa is finally back where it rightfully belongs - competing for `Best of the 60's Concept Albums.' Odessa is a symphonic tragedy of love and loss at sea. The original album had an  elegant and luxurious velvet cover. Technological innovation has negated  the cover, but the sophistication and grandeur of the music  remain.Melody and harmony are the Bee Gees strong suit. `Black Diamond,'  `Melody Fair,' and `Lamplight' challenge the most infectious  Lennon-McCartney melodies. Maurice, Barry and Robin share lead vocals.  Maurice and Barry are provocative on the more whimsical stuff (Edison,  Melody Fair, I Laugh In Your Face). Barry sings naturally - he's no  pathetic castrado here. And Robin's nasal vibrato is ideal for the love  songs (Black Diamond, Lamplight, First of May). If the Everly Brothers own  the patent on flawless sibling harmony, then the Bee Gees borrowed it for  Odessa. Their harmonies are dazzling.On a literal note, the majority of  the lyrics are nonsensical: `It took a thousand years to find out why  you'll never see my face again,' and `my brother is friendly for reasons if  I am the same just for four hundred seasons we all live in rain.' Matter  not. You'll sing them regardless. Odessa is a mushy and overblown sixty  minutes of beauty, tragedy and love.

reviewText: Probably the best band under the trip-hop genre, Massive Attack outdo themselves with this terrific and hypnotic album. Certainly one of the best records of the late nineties and much likely the best trip-hop release ever, "Mezzanine" is an excellent dark album, truly captivating an intriguing end-of-the-milennium atmosphere.Massive Attacks`s third effort is more rock-oriented than their previous ones, relying on the strenght of guitars. Still, the electronic elements play a big role as well, as the band again uses a lot of loops and samples to create and absorbing and at times claustrophobic mood. Each song is a complex and addictive moment and none of them lack distinction. This is a strong and compelling record without any filler. The opener "Angel", sung by frequent collaborator Horace Andy, starts in a smooth and subtle note to end with an amazing guitar explosion that makes for a perfect beginning to the album. Other highlights (even if it`s difficult to choose highlights here) include the gorgeous first single "Teardrop", the spooky and unsettling "Inertia Creeps", the superbly dark and nightmarish "Man Next Door" or the unusual and haunting "Group Four"."Mezzanine" is by far Massive Attack`s best release, a multilayered and diverse record which carries an hypnotic nocturnal feel, presenting songs full of tension, mysteries and countless details. This album offers something new and unique with each listen, becoming vicious and a true must-own. It also has something for everyone, as it is difficult not to like at least one or two songs here (I think they`re all great, even the instrumental "Exchange").One of the best records of the last decade.

reviewText: I have to say I was a bit disappointed with Clays album, but after listening to it a few more times, its starting to grow on me. There's no doubt that Clay has one of the best voices in pop music today. His crystal clear tenor sounds effortless. However, it doesn't translate as well on cd than it did live on American Idol.The cd as a whole is a bit redundant. Most of the songs sound alike, and a few of the songs sound familiar to some songs recorded by other artists. With that said though, there a plenty to choose from that made this album enjoyable. First single, Invisible, is a catchy pop tune that instantly grabs your attention. The power ballads No More Sad Songs and Measure of a Man are beautiful that really showcases Clays powerful pipes. A Perfect Day could be a song from the 80's but Clay sings it with such charsima and energy that it makes for one of the best songs on the album.I don't criticize Clays performance, he truly is an amazing talent, its the music that doesn't do his voice justice. While alot of people were highly anticipating this album, it came out to soon. Kelly Clarkson waited 9 months and released a remarkable, diverse album. An album that obviously had a lot of time and effort put into it. Clay's album was rushed, and it seems like the producers just gave him some songs to sing without picking and choosing the best ones. I look forward to Clays 2nd effort, were hopefully he'll have more input and an oppurtunity to show us what he's all about and that will let his talent shine through.

reviewText: I recently picked up a used copy of "Home Before Dark."  Neil Diamond's more recent work has sometimes pitched to epic arrangements and bombastic vocals, which I have not found quite as moving as his earlier work.  However, this disc bowls me over, intimate and moving.  The opening track "If I Don't See You Again" haunts with the passion of a relationship interrupted, "What's it going to come to baby; Who you gonna hide behind when the nights get filled up with doom?"  "Pretty Amazing Grace" is another powerful track that could be about a flawed lover recognizing the value of his love or it could be about faith found.  "Forgotten" has a retro melody that is delightful, even without a prominent drummer.  "No Words" is another glorious pop nugget with an unplugged type of arrangement that puts a smile on my face.  "Home Before Dark" is a great return to form from this musical legend.  Enjoy!

reviewText: The Red Hot Chili Peppers seem to be a bit less "Red Hot" these days. They're still making very good music, but it seems that they have mellowed with age. Just compare Californication to Mother's Milk, The Uplift Mofo Party Plan or even Blood Sugar Sex Magik and you'll see that the RHCPs have definitely chilled out a bit. Pretty much gone is the frantic funk-rap-rock style of earlier days, now the Peppers seem more interested in crafting pretty melodies. This is a much more radio-friendly group than the one that brought us "Give It Away", "Power Of Equality" and "Sir Psycho Sexy".I think Californication is a good album with a lot of great songs, but frankly it just doesn't rock enough. Compared with Blood Sugar Sex Magik which had great songs, a tight groove, plenty of hard-rockers, a lot of funk, and a very high energy level, Californication seems sedated in comparison. Not that that's bad, it's just a new direction for the band. However, I must say that I prefer the old Chili Peppers. There are a few tracks on the album that approach the funky rockin' style of Blood Sugar Sex Magik such as "Around The World", "I Like Dirt" and "Get On Top", but it's mostly polished pop/rock without much of a trace of the Peppers' distinct style.Californication is certainly one of their better albums, but fans of the old-school Chili Peppers may be a bit dismayed. Many of the songs sound tailor-made for radio and are missing that late 80s/early 90s energy. This is a fine album, and I'm glad it was a success, but Blood Sugar Sex Magik went platinum many times over without the benefit of such a radio-friendly sound, and even with the disadvantage of an "explicit lyrics" sticker (meaning no Wal-Mart sales).I enjoy this album, but when I want a taste of the real Red Hot Chili Peppers, I will cue up Mother's Milk or Blood Sugar Sex Magik.

There are a few tracks on the album that approach the funky rockin' style of Blood Sugar Sex Magik such as "Around The World", "I Like Dirt" and "Get On Top", but it's mostly polished pop/rock without much of a trace of the Peppers' distinct style.Californication is certainly one of their better albums, but fans of the old-school Chili Peppers may be a bit dismayed. Many of the songs sound tailor-made for radio and are missing that late 80s/early 90s energy. This is a fine album, and I'm glad it was a success, but Blood Sugar Sex Magik went platinum many times over without the benefit of such a radio-friendly sound, and even with the disadvantage of an "explicit lyrics" sticker (meaning no Wal-Mart sales).I enjoy this album, but when I want a taste of the real Red Hot Chili Peppers, I will cue up Mother's Milk or Blood Sugar Sex Magik.

reviewText: Watch out, pop tarts, 'cause Imogen Heap has returned.This singer made a little-noticed debut seven years ago, with "I Megaphone." In the meantime, she became half of the mega-successful Frou Frou, though it was only intended as a side-project. Now she has returned with her second solo album, an energetic and sparkling piece of pop: "Speak For Yourself."The album kicks off with the entrancing "Headlock," where music-box pop blossoms out into dark pop splendour. That sets the tone for the rest of the album, following it up with entrancing instrumentation, velvety melodies, and a few hooks to draw you into the songs. There's even a few rock numbers, like the explosive bass of "Daylight Robbery." You go girl.After seven years off the radar, it's to be expected that Heap's musical style would change. It does, and it's good. She started off as a sort of Tori Amos-style young angry woman, playing guitar and venting her spleen. But in this album, she evokes nobody except her own self.It may seem that her acid-tinged style has simply softened up, but such is not the case. She's not taunting old bullies and ragging on people who invade her personal space. Instad she's disdainfully telling an evasive lover: "You say too late to start/with your heart in a headlock/You know your better than this!"But she has not lost her sharper edge. "No, it's not meant to be like this/It's just what I don't need/Why make me feel like this?/It's definitely all your fault!" Her sound isn't that of an Angry Young Woman, ripping into people who have done her wrong. Instead, she sounds more mature -- her heart has been broken, her lovers have been untrue, but she can still get excited about new love.Her musical style has mellowed as well, even more than her writing. Being in Frou Frou seems to have influenced her solo style, mingling the piano with tinkling melodies and swirling synth. And her velvety voice soars over all of it, able to sink into a worn-out whisper, or rise into a throaty roar.Heap makes a mark on her second album, with a unique brand of swirling, intricate pop, and her lovely voice. "Speak For Yourself" is energetic, elaborate, and enormous fun.

reviewText: A year later, this is still one of the best CDs out right now.  Eric Benet finds a way to bring classic soul into the new millenium.  His first CD, "True To Myself" brought the hits "Let's Stay  Together", "Femininity", "All In The Game" and  "While You Were Here".  "A Day In The Life" takes place  where his last CD left off, which is a good thing.  The whole CD is  excellent and a must own for true r&b fans.  The highlights include the  current single and my favorite track on the CD, "When You Think Of  Me" w/Roy Ayres.  This song has Eric telling a former girlfriend it's  nice that you're thinking of me now, but if you would've took care of your  business in the first place I wouldn't be singing this song. Other  highlights include "Love The Hurt Away", "That's Just My  Way", the first single "Georgy Porgy" w/Faith Evans, and one  of the best slow jams of 1999, "Spend My life With You" w/Tamia.  Also check out "The Best Man" soundtrack for his song  "Poetry Girl", which is one of the best songs on the soundtrack.  Eric Benet definitely was not a victim of the sophomore jinx, he's just  getting better with time.

reviewText: Let me be up front:  I hate the metal/rap garbage that started becoming mainstream in the late '90s even more than the overall grunge scene annoyed me earlier in that decade.  Many of the rock bands I like from today may be considered "safe" (e.g., Creed, matchbox twenty, Goo Goo Dolls), but that is simply because there has not been a great rock music trend since heavy metal became mainstream in the 1980s.  The above-mentioned bands are at least accessible to someone my age, as they combine some of the best elements from various eras of rock music.  That being said, this album by this band has truly hit me the right way.  I certainly never thought I'd like an album that has the "record scratch" sound in it.  This band has changed that, much like the Red Hot Chili Pepers allowed me to appreciate music with rapping in it 10 years ago (with their "Blood Sugar Sex Magic" album) even though I hate rap music overall.What I like about this album is that it is both rocking and mellow--a diverse collection, and the sound is accessible.  My favorite bands from the past can be both hard and soft effectively, and this band does this as well with a modern twist.  I love the mid-tempo track and big rock radio hit "Wish You Were Here".  "Nice To Know You" and "Warning" are other tracks that have improved the quality of what is on rock radio.  "Circles" and "Under My Umbrella" are other great rockers, and "11am", "Mexico", and especially the long closing track "Aqueous Transmission" bring this band into mellow territory that suits them very well.I wasn't privy to this band's earliest releases; I admittedly became aware of them with the "Make Yourself" release and their big radio single "Drive".  While that album was decent overall, this one is even better--a truly listenable rock CD.  Call my overall rating 4 1/4 stars for a fine and diverse modern rock record that, while somewhat mainstream, doesn't cater to any particular current trend.  Very enjoyable.

reviewText: By 1982 Adam Ant had ditched his band The Ants and gone solo. "Friend Or Foe" was his first solo album and probably his best. Following off the mega-success of his previous album "Prince Charming", he and Marco, the only band member he kept, came up with another brilliantly catchy and fun album. Again, in America, unfortunately only "Goody Two Shoes" hit the top 40. There are other greats here, and again, like "Prince Charming", not a wasted note. "Friend Or Foe", "Place In The Country", "Desperate But Not Serious", "Here Comes The Grump", a cover of The Doors' "Hello I Love You", "Crackpot History And The Right To Lie" are all great!Besides the original 12 tracks you also get an overwhelming 12 bonus tracks, most of which are demo versions of album tracks and forgettable. There's not much difference between the Chris Hughes mix of "Goody Two Shoes" and the original. "Coup d'Etat" was only okay. "And So You Shall" as a demo is funny and shows promise. It's too bad it didn't make a final version. "Yellowbeard" is average fare, same with "I Know They Know" and "Gargoyles Are A Go". "Good Sex Rumples The Clothing" is actually amusing and catchy though it sounds like a blueprint for "Crackpot History And The Right To Lie".Again, the lyrics come with the booklet and the graphic design and artwork ties in nicely with the other remasters in this series. All in all, another great album!

reviewText: What can you really say about Amerikkka's Most Wanted? The CD speaks for itself. This is the first Cube solo effort. He is fresh out of NWA, but he doesn't waste his time talking about the breakup. Cube comes out with a lot to say and he does it well.Cube addresses most modern issues facing the black community. From Oreo cookies, to sellouts with phd's, to the projects; Cube has it all. The raps are extremely viable statements. Unlike most rappers, Cube doesn't come out with paper-thin excuses that pass the buck. He addresses legit issues with legit attitudes. I will reiterate that Cube has the intelligence to be a civil rights leader. The cat has a gift for rhyme and a penchant for telling it like it is. I give the lyrics my highest recommendation.That said, Cube can also make you laugh. "You Can't Fade Me" is a classic about Cube having a pregnancy scare. At one point in the song he fantasizes about booting the ho in the stomach. The whole song, including the beat, is really one of the funniest rap songs ever made. It also has the classic "JD's Gafflin'" at the end and that is top notch.Unfortunately, it's not all good. The bottom line is that it's 11 years later. The beats and even the rapping are a bit dated. I won't dwell on it because it's not fair to review it 11 years later. Let's just say the beats are adequate but quite dated compared to today's standards. If you don't like old rap you will not dig this CD. Some people hear a certain sound and they're already off it. If you aren't willing to give it a shot, you'll hate it.There are also some songs that just aren't very good. "What They Hittin Fo'?", "A Gangsra's Fairytale", and "It's a Man's World" are pretty much just poor efforts. You could probably find a couple more if you looked a little closer or were not as big a fan of Cube as me. The CD is a definite mix of excellent, good and bad. Cube's best and worst are all on display on this album.Boy, it's hard to conclude the review. If you dig rap that's all about the bling bling and Bentleys this is not for you. If you like new hot raps that are smooth as silk this is not for you. If you are all about a nice sounding rap this is not for you. If you like some old school conscious rap than this CD is a must have.

reviewText: This is the official 1998 CD edition of the first-ever Robert Johnson compilation, issued by Columbia in 1961.It has been remastered off the best-quality original 78s available, and Johnson's guitar takes on a fullness never heard on previous reissues (the equalization on this disc is extreme to a degree where it even sports some minute turntable rumble in the low end).I still say that there is no really good reason to buy this CD instead of Columbia's 1990 box set "The Complete Recordings", but if you are looking for a single-disc overview, this one has almost all of Johnson's best songs (with the notable exception of "Sweet Home Chicago" and "I Believe I'll Dust My Broom"), and the sound quality is truly amazing. I have the box set, but I also have this CD, actually. The remastering is that good.

reviewText: i can't get enough of this album! released way back in 1998, hard knock life would be jay-z's best all-around album. i say this because, even though reasonable doubt was tremendous, it had lame beats compared to this, where all the tracks are fire. "hand it down" starts off the album with a memphis bleek freestyle. i honestly find it hard to believe he freestyled this because with memph man, it's all down hill from here (he's a weak lyricist aside from this track). next is "hard knock life" the main single. this is a very hot song and was definately innovative at the time. following that are my 2 favorite tracks "if i should die" where jay and da ranjahz spit ridiculously, and "ride or die" which has superb lyrics, a tight beat, and a subliminal ma$e diss. "n what n who" shows jay-z taking on that chicago sniper type rhyming (think twista) and he delivers a blazing song (4th single from album). after that i believe is "money cash hoes" with dmx and one of the hottest beats i've heard from swizz. song's title is self-explanatory. next is "a week ago" the second collabo jay-z had with too short. this song is a great storytelling thing about snitching. on the second side of the album invites us to see memph bleek again who engages jay-z in a back and forth dialogue between hustlas in "coming of age 2". thanks to swizz the beat was spectacular. next is "paper chase" which is a very hot timbaland track featuring the always sexy and hard spitting fox boogie brown. it's basically talking about a bank robbery and all. nice song. following that i believe is the 3rd single "can i get a..." which was constantly being played on z100 (which sucks...thanks tools) but nevertheless is a back and forth braggadoccio battle between amil and jay-z. also this introduced us to the infamous ja rule. i don't care what anyone says, ja rule is a pretty good lyricist. somewhere after that is "resevoir dogs" which was dissed by the amazon.com reviewer. the guy is stupid for saying that this was filler. ok, the lox, beanie, sauce money, and jay-z spit the most memorable verses i've heard from ALL of them. thanks, sermon, for the shaft beat; that makes the track even hotter! reviewText: Back in the late 60's, the sister and brother duo consisting of Richard and Karen Carpenter, known as The Carpenters were one of the seventies best loved groups.  Their first hit "Ticket To Ride" (a Beatles hit), released in 1969 did moderately well for their label A&M, but it wasn't until 1970 that the song "(They Long To Be) Close To You" shot straight up the charts to number one followed a few months later with another hit "We've Only Just Begun". The following year produced yet more hits for The Carpenters with "Superstar", "Rainy Days And Mondays" and "For All We Know", establishing The Carpenters as one of the most popular groups of the early seventies. Throughout the decade the hits continued and The Carpenters had accumulated 10 gold singles and 11 gold albums in the United States. This 2-cd "Gold: 35th Anniversary Edition" includes all their great hits such as the above mentioned songs as well as "Only Yesterday", "Please Mr. Postman", "There A Kind Of A Hush (All Over The World)", "Top Of The World", "Yesterday Once More", and a rare version of "California Dreaming" (originally a hit for The Mamas & Papas) as well as a remake of the Canadian rock group Klatuu's "Calling Occupants Of Interplanetary Craft" plus many more (40 songs total). This collection has been remastered and remixed and sounds great, the clarity of the instruments and vocals is astonishing. Also, included is a ten page booklet with a few colorful photos and a song by song breakdown and explanation by Richard Carpenter himself. Sadly, Karen Carpenter passed away in 1983 at age 32 and the world lost one of music's most gifted and beautiful voices ever. If you enjoyed the great music the seventies gave us from artists such as The Carpenters, Bread and Three Dog Night to name just a few, then this collection is a must have.

reviewText: When I first bought this album, I thought it would be a new type of food product. Maybe it was because they had way better name for the titles of their albums. I mean, why kinda name is Chocolate Starfish and the Hot Dog Flavored Water?! Limp Bizkit shouldent confuse us like that! This album is kind of boring too. Theres not many good songs here. Even some songs that are supposed to be serious (like "Boiler") have some silly lyrics like "No eating no sleeping just giving into you and i'm dumb". Why are you gonna starve yourself out, Fred, when you can eat chocolate starfish and drink hotdog flavored water? I just don't undertstand. My favorite song on this album is 'Hold On'. This was very dissapointing. Buyers beware: this product might not be what your looking for. Get it expecting a not so great Limp Bizkit album. Don't get it looking for chocolate starfish and hot dog flavored water. Hey, at least I know why they don't sell it in super markets...

reviewText: Taking in account how many fantastic live recordings there excist of Phil Collins, with Genesis and solo, it's really surprising how dull and uninspiring this, the only official release from his solo career, is. It's now bad, but the performance isn't exceptional by any means, and the sound is unsatisfying.The are a couple of songs on this recording, that I think is what it all should have been like - 'Do You Remember' is very beautiful (though very close to the album version - more interesting is perhaps the piano-only version from his 1997 tour). 'In The Air Tonight' is good, but also this one was done better later - check out the 'Live And Loose In Paris' video from the 1997 tour. 'Take Me Home' is here in a great prolonged version, and is one of the highlights of the set.Many of the uptempo songs - 'Something Happened...', 'Who Said I Would' and especially 'Sussudio' suffers from a somewhat metallic sound, making them less enjoyable than other recordings.All in all, this is a nice record with some great songs, but most of them suffers from the "not as good as..." problem. If you think this is fantastic, try to get the 1997 video ... or some of the full recordings from either 1994 or 1997 tour - now THAT is great! And why the [heck] weren't any of those released as offical CDs?

reviewText: If one were to pick among the many excellent recordings by the late guitarist Grant Green, this one would be it!!  If not for the very long title track written by Duke Pearson with a kind of MJQ flavor to it, this would still be a classic recording since it boasts an all star line up of Bobby Hutcherson, vibes, Joe Henderson on tenor, Duke Pearson on piano and Green on guitar, who all perform at the top of their game. Pearson himself is responsible for the success of this classic since not only did he pen the title track but also two winners such as "Jean DeFleur" (based on Laura) and "Nomad". But one cannot forget the memorable title track plus the inspired playing of Green and associates.  This album plus "Solid" which also has Henderson in the lineup is fully recommended for Green fans.

reviewText: According to Phil Spector himself, "I would say I'm probably relatively insane, to an extent.  I take medication for schizophrenia, but I wouldn't say I'm schizophrenic. But I have a bipolar personality, which is strange. I'm my own worst enemy. I have devils inside that fight me."And yet:  In his prime, he made some of the most joyfully soothing music you've ever heard.  It's like Brian Wilson, who also used the pure magic of music to both soothe himself and then share that loving gesture with the world.You know how it is at Christmas.  It's supposed to be a season of giving, but instead it is a season of intense pressure, during which we are exposed routinely to what is worst about American consumer society.  So imagine you're sitting in a long line of cars, trying to get into or out of an immense mall parking lot.  You're thinking, "Why do we do this?  Just so department stores can make their margins?  Just so our kids can satisfy their lust for what they've seen advertised on TV? Why?"  And then, if you are listening to the right station, one of the tunes from this album comes on.  I don't know about you, but every time I hear Spector's version of "White Christmas" or "Sleigh Ride" or "Marshmallow World" or--especially--"Baby Please Come Home," my mind and spirit are eased, I'm smiling at the inherent humor and absurdity behind it all, and I'm looking forward to sitting by the fire with my family and hearing the whole album.  Darlene Love's performance of "Baby Please Come Home" has become a tradition on the David Letterman show --almost the only TV Christmas tradition I buy into totally.As I write, Spector's demons have apparently, allegedly, finally caught up with him, and that's sad and pathetic.  But out of his madness, there were pure musical gestures that he made, like this album, that were true gifts to the soul and spirit.  Go get it.
summary: Balm for the insane at an insane season

reviewText: This album is one of her best and displays an angry side of Tori not shown before. In this album, Tori is very angry and frustrated, because at the time of making the album, she and her boyfriend/producer Eric Rosse parted  ways, and she's taking her anger and frustration out in her music, namely  in this album, 'Boys For Pele'. An excellent example of this is the song  "Professional Widow"; she is just pissed off in this nicely-done  song. All of the songs on this marvelous album get me, but one song in  particular that gets me in a melancholy chord is "Not The Red  Baron". It is a superb, superb, sad song of hers that is infinitely  hard to be outdone. The short songs are excellent as well and have a beauty  to them all their own. There are even a few songs that seem to discreetly  indicate that her and Eric broke up, like in the lyrics for  'Hey  Jupiter'....."No One's Picking Up The Phone...guess it's clear...he's  gone.....".

reviewText: Burn is often overlooked because there's no Gillan. Don't be one of the people who ignore this album. Everything is good. The first track rocks from start to finish, and the band never lets up. Even my (comparatively) least favorite track, "Lay Down, Stay Down," is pretty good. "Sail Away" is the next best song to "Burn," but doesn't recieve much recognition for some odd reason. If you've heard recordings of "Mistreated" live, i.e., California Jam or Made in Europe, you might be a bit disappointed in the studio version, but it's still excellent. All in all a masterpiece. Highly recommended.

reviewText: After the dynamite debut of their "Dreamboat Annie" album (and the unofficial "Magazine," Heart went for the bulls eye on "Little Queen." From the explosive opener "Barracuda," you'd be thinking they had pulled it off. With a riff so distinctive (there was a guitar pedal named after the downbending sound in the opening chords), the band's proclomation that they were somewhere between Led Zepplin and a folk act seemed to be coming true.Well, almost. Despite the cover of "Stairway To Heaven (Live)" as a bonus track, Heart was still feeling out their potential. As a rocker, "Kick it Out" is about halfway there, but the folkie plucking of "Love Alive" captures the band at a high point. "Little Queen" also contains some of Heart's better compositions, like the title track and "Dream Of The Archer." Ann's voice is powerful and guitarist Roger Fisher (who co-wrote most of the songs) has that Jimmy Page thing down pat."Little Queen" may not be Heart's best (IMHO, that goes to "Dog and Butterfly") but it is a must have for fans of the band, along with "Dreamboat Annie." This is still the raucous Heart, before the 80's polished them up and laid in the syntesizers for "Heart" (featuring "Alone").

reviewText: Listening to the album more and more, I'm really late in writing this review and to a sad fare, nobody will ever really cast the attention I'd really want on it. But, whatever, two cents is worth, well...less than that. Anyway, I'm a modest person, so I'll write for free. In conclusion, the album is easily one of the most influential this entire year.Closing the album out with 'Leech' was a fine move, but following a ballad like 'Here in My Room' is a hard task. The song is so full of emotion, and no, I don't mean that in anyway like people claim most music today. This emotion doesn't lie in the fact that Brandon sings "deep", it's how he writes it lyrically and the way he sings it, sounds as if it's coming off scratch, off the top of his head. You don't generally hear that a lot in music, in fact, you never hear that. All in all, the songs are really tightly formed, the best of Incubus.'Pistola' is easily the best song off the album. I say this because it's one of the more different songs of Incubus. It sounds like a classic 70's jam with Brandon Boyd. The lyrics are clever and the bass line follows nicely with the guitar work that create such a 'bad ass' song. I can only see myself driving constantly to that song, wishing I was driving off ramps, and chasing something rather than trying to make it back on time to work. An easy favorite. 'Priceless' is such a throwback to early alternative, I applaud the band. The music scene today is so dry and the same old same old, with leeches everywhere making music just like the other person. Throwbacks are always good, yet unorginal at times, but the Incubus team fare away from this, and create a new song with that 'vibe.' Standing freakin' ovation.'Agoraphobia' is easily the most lacking of the album, with the repetitive chorus, I always skip it usually. It's a fine song, but for the entirity of the album, I could do without it. The lyrics are good, but unfinished seeminly, I can see Boyd writing this at a jam, with the awaiting band staring and saying, "Well..." and Boyd going with what he had, using filler. This doesn't stunt the album, but it is sure noticeable. 'Talk Show on Mute' has another throwback with synthesizers that spark Thomas Dolby or other popular 80's icons...it's a nice change and since I'm an avid fan of hating the 80's music, I'm glad I can finally enjoy it somewhat, by liking this song. Rounding out the beginning, 'A Crow Left of the Murder', along with 'Pistola' later mentioned, is probably the best song on the album. The guitar is catchy, the drums are stellar, no pun intended, and the vocals are some of Boyd's finest work.When 'Megolomaniac' came on the air, I was a bit disappointed the boys of Incubus went political. But then again, at least they're saying a message. Most of the music today, and no I'm not in my late sixties and embarking on the past, is horrible and goes nowhere. This song has such a great introduction, that you know the album is taking you for a ride, and once the guitar really kicks in, as well as the band, you know you're riding high. A powerhouse song and a good single to tell people to f*cking listen to you.Incubus has been on my list of bands that I don't claim as favorites, but bands I look at, and wait for. Enjoying heavily upon the release of 'Make Yourself', I was disappointed to see the road they went with an almost boy band image on teen magazines with the debut of 'Drive.' Was Boyd this full of himself? The raging reggae, dredlock man? Then...'Morning View' came out and I was established with an answer, 'yes.' Besides 'Mexico', 'Aqueuos Transmissions', and 'Warning', the band had taken 'Drive' and created an entire album. I was threw with the band and to my surprise, note the sarcasm, the band took off in an entire different way. So, they were on the back burner, but I waited for what they had in their kitchen. The result, one of the most acclaimed albums since The Strokes 'Room on Fire' and Blink-182's self titled, 'A Crow Left of the Murder.' With the release of the aforementioned albums, I am pretty sure music may be taking a softer turn, slowly, and surely. The Paul McCartney's of the past are now Dave Grohl's, and the influential sounds are being taken into effect by those that have learned. Incubus is one of those bands, they are evolving, they are changing, and this album is a direct result to this. And yeah, for many who may understand this, they're 'keeping it real.'This review is going to be a little long.
summary: A Band Left of the Music

reviewText: I haven't been able to stop playing this album. I'm a big fan of Foxy Brown, and it has been a long time coming since she released her last album. Though regarded as a "mixtape/street album" people will still associate this with an album since it had a commercial release. Due to Foxy's incarceration last year, Foxy wasn't able to fully promote this album. When she was released, she wasn't too happy with the final product. That sucks! I like the album! Though its not by any means my favorite album but it knocks regardless. Casual fans of Foxy won't understand this release if they haven't followed Fox like longtime fans. I would definitely say this album is worth checking out for what its worth. It's not everyday we get any type of album for a female rapper. My hats off to Foxy for keeping female rap alive.Favorite/Recommended Tracks:"Never Heard This Before""Too Real""Dreams...""Star Cry""Why"

reviewText: This is the first album (CD) I have ever purchased, and it turned out to be a great album!  My father had a great collection of Billy Joel works through the 70's, 80's, and 90's.  But, for some reason he didn't have this album; I guess "The Stranger" over shadowed this album!I really have to thank Billy Joel because it was this album that really made me indulge into music.  He puts a lot of effort musically as well as lyrically, making all of his works unforgetable.  How can you forget, "Scenes at the Italian Restaurant" for an example.Now, this album "Turnstiles" is a classic work!  There is no question about that. The album has a good flow to it; all the songs come together well, one song doesn't over show the others.  Again the lyrics are awesome here, you can't get away with not learning new words with his complex lyrics.Many would call "Piano Man" his break through album, but personally his real master work "Turnstiles" is what gave Billy Joel worldwide attention and fame by setting the plateform for the "The Stranger."  Although "Piano Man" acquired more attention, his "Turnstilles" album performs better if you give it time.If you don't have this album, it's a must get.  Out of all Billy Joel works, it's among the few that stands up to "The Stranger."

reviewText: In my mind, "Love Box" pales a wee bit in comparison to its 2001 predecessor, "Goodbye Country (Hello Nightclub)," but that doesn't mean Groove Armada's latest isn't noteworthy.  It is.  They bring on the funk on smooth cuts like the aptly named "Groove Is On," and they spin the disco ball on house-ed up jams like "Final Shakedown," "Easy," and the title track.  But for me, "Love Box" is a noteable record because it marks the return of the gone-but-mostly-forgotten Neneh Cherry, who lends her voice on the piano-laced slow jam "Think Twice."  But there's no need to "think twice" about getting this disc.  Groove Armada have been leaders in smart, beat-heavy electro pop, and they've released a party of an album worth crashing.  Open the "box," and jump in.
summary: Groove Armada is Back! (And They Brought Neneh With Them)
filteredReviewText: In my mind, "Love Box" pales a wee bit in comparison to its 2001 predecessor, "Goodbye Country (Hello Nightclub)," but that doesn't mean Groove Armada's latest isn't noteworthy. They bring on the funk on smooth cuts like the aptly named "Groove Is On," and they spin the disco ball on house-ed up jams like "Final Shakedown," "Easy," and the title track. But for me, "Love Box" is a noteable record because it marks the return of the gone-but-mostly-forgotten Neneh Cherry, who lends her voice on the piano-laced slow jam "Think Twice." But there's no need to "think twice" about getting this disc. Groove Armada have been leaders in smart, beat-heavy electro pop, and they've released a party of an album worth crashing.

reviewText: Amazingly agile with both the English language and musical instrumentation, and  possessing a healthy grasp of world history, Ezra Koenig, specifically, Rostam Batmanglij (and the band) have come up with an instance classic worthy of, and the equal to, such institutions as Sgt. Pepper's, Revolver, Innervisions and any other of the variety of albums which are on course for very long lives and hyperbolic interjections of newly-found appreciation.  What is more amazing than the band's ability to pull a classic together, is their capacity to realize the grievous error of their sophomore effort, a less ingratiating aping of a musical institution (Paul Simon) one is hard pressed to find. If I have had any reservations about the band, they have been erased by this treasure, pulled from the fire before almost inevitable conflagration (of the band), and duly submitted to the public for the approval of at least a smattering of it.

reviewText: By now, the formula is firmly established: funky, pile-driving bass, tasty guitar licks and kick-ass kick-drums. On top of that, Fagen's distinctive wry vocalizing. I like this album (although some songs just go on too long, What I Do being Exhibit A), but I'm wondering if this represents artistic progress for Fagen. Too formulaic, similar tempos and unvarying harmonic palette (although that palette does shine nicely here).The funk-band side of Steely Dan first appeared on Aja and took full root with Gaucho. Pretzel Logic and Gaucho represent two wholly dissimilar approaches to the rhythm section and I know which one I prefer. My question is: now that Fagen probably has all the money he needs why does he persist with these cookie-cutter tunes? Has he abdicated bebop? And even rock and roll, for that matter?

reviewText: This album is not as good as I thought it would be, but it isn't all that bad either. There are some gems that make it a keeper. We Live This, which features the return of the old-school legend, Roxanne Shante, is one the bangers on this compilation. Find Ya Wealth is a year-old gem from Nas. Street Glory pairs Nas up with Pops, who is kind of impressive on the mic. We Break Bread is another standout tracks where Craig G steals the show in the last verse. Fire and Pile Raps are highlights as well, but I think that one of the most compelling tracks on the album is Self-Conscience with Nas and Prodigy. The tracks that I just mentioned are worth the price of the album alone. The album does have a few mis-steps, but overall, it is a good compilation. Nas' lyrics that up the slack were some of the album's guest fall short. I recommend this.

reviewText: The spotty "Boy with the Arab Strap" was a major letdown mainly because the excellence of this, its predecessor, set such a high standard for this band. If you haven't heard Belle & Sebastian, be warned that  if fey, heavily Scottish singing isn't your cup of tea, it'll turn you off  the way Morrissey's voice made a lot of people dislike the Smiths even if  they enjoyed the music. This album has B&S' most incisive, funny  lyrics, pastoral arrangements (the Vince Guaraldi-esque "Seeing Other  People" is a particular standout), and sharpest songwriting. The only  clunker in the bunch, in my opinion, is the wheezy "The Boy Done Wrong  Again." One of the best British indie releases of the past few years.

reviewText: No matter what you think of Ms. Winehouse's eccentric and in your face image, such as the bee-hive hair, the tatoos, and excessive drinking, you have to give her props: the girl can sing. Not only that, but she knows what the hell she is singing about. She's not trying to show off her pipes or show that she's "dirrty," she simply sings about issues that are real to her. Overall, the album is solid and by far one of the best albums of 2007. However, my only complaint about this CD and Ms. Winehouse is that I wish there was more diversity in what she sings about. Singing about sex, drugs, and bad men is fine, but to dedicate a whole album to it eventually gets kind of old, uninspiring, and drawn out way too much. After the first 3 tracks, the whole album starts to sound like one entire song about the same thing: drugs, weed, bad men, and sex. Hopefully the girl will show the world what she's really all about, still be herself, but show some more depth to her image.

reviewText: "Peachtree Road" got a glowing review that termed it a fitting follow-up to Songs from the West Coast; so I ran out and grabbed it!  -- Maybe I should've waited to read a few more reviews.  This isn't a bad set; it's just faceless.  My favorite track is "Too Many Tears" with its pulsing rhythms and John's creative work on keyboards, "Did you go to Dallas on that day?  Have you been to where they broke a dream, where there really isn't room for doubt, somehow we got lost and the truth is buried somewhere in between."  Some of the tracks are pretty good like the slow but sweet "It's Getting Dark in Here" and "Answer in the Sky" that has some pep, although the lyrics seem a bit obvious.  Three tunes in the middle are ones I want to skip.  "My Elusive Drug" is depressing; "They Call Her the Cat" comes across as tacky for no reason, and "Freaks In Love" has a pulse but little else going for it.  "Turn the Lights Out When You Leave" relies on the title as if it were a tremendously clever lyric rather than a tired cliche.  All in all, even when Elton is average, he's still worth listening to.  Don't expect too much and let yourself enjoy what's here.  If there's an answer in the sky, perhaps we could get Elton a bigger telescope.  Next!

reviewText: Alright let me start by saying, how dope is that cover? I mean it's nothing special, it's just him wit a mean mug on, but I don't know I just really like it. Alright so this is Jeezy's fourth project and we all know how much this has been pushed back. Almost to the point where it became annoying. And in turn it kind of killed my hype for the album. But it's here, so that's all that counts right?From his last album to the release of this one we've seen Jeezy release a string of mostly mediocre mixtapes, with a dope one every now and then. We've also seen him release a bunch of promotional singles. Some which are on the Deluxe Edition, some which were left off entirely. As a whole the album really isn't all that bad. Is it his best work? No. Is it a proper follow up to "The Recession"? Honestly, no.Production wise it's your typical southern album. In terms of subject matter it's like his first 2 albums. He has some songs about drinkin', drugs, sex, him just spittin' bars, and a deep song or two. But in today's world that's honestly nothing new. But it works. I mean for Jeezy it just works. He's one of those rappers that you can't expect too much from. You just expect some dope music. And that's what he does on this album, for the most part.A couple things I found odd/terrible. Track 13 "Higher Learning (Feat. Snoop Dogg, Devin The Dude & Mitchellel)" obviously it's a track about smoking weed, but it's just bad. It throws off the whole flow of the album. So I'm glad it was at the end. Track 10 "Trapped (Feat. Jill Scott)" it had potential to be my favorite song on the album, but there's two sections where Jill Scott tries to... I guess we can say "rap" and it's terrible. At the very begining of the song before Jeezy comes in she has one of these "rap" section and she says "whack sauce". "Whack sauce"? Really? Every time I hear the song and she says that I cringe. And it's sad because she does amazing on the hook, but whatever.Standout Songs: "Waiting" & "F.A.M.E. (Feat. T.I.)"Overall Score: 7/10 - In short it's a nice Jeezy album. It's Jeezy doing his thing, and for the most part it's what we've come to expect from him. As I've said before I don't feel it's a proper follow up album to "The Recession" but I'll just wait patiently for him to make another album like that.

reviewText: This 2 disc Greatest Hits is the ultimate collection of Mariah's best songs up to 2000. This collection covers ballads, dance tracks, and Hip-Hop and R&B; jams. It features 10 years worth of material from the most beautiful voice to ever be heard!Vision Of Love was Mariah's very first song ever released and it also became her very first number 1 on the Billboard Hot 100. I totally love the hauntingly, beautiful intro in this amazing ballad. Vision Of Love is from the album Mariah Carey, from 1990.Love Takes Time is a very beautiful, slow ballad which became Mariah's 2nd #1 on Billboard. Love Takes Time is also from the debut album, Mariah Carey, from 1990.Someday was actually the very first song that I heard from her debut and once I heard it MTV or VH1, I just totally fell in love with it for that really high note that she does at the end! I actually prefer the music video/Jackswing versions best because of the unique music and her high note rather than the album version which doesn't really let you hear that high note because the song fades out. But this album version is still cool and it became Mariah's 3rd #1 from the Mariah Carey album from 1990.I Don't Wanna Cry is my all time favorite ballad from the Mariah Carey album from 1990. I just love the way Mariah sings and the music itself is amazing! This became Mariah's 4th #1.The song Emotions broke a record as it was the 5th consecutive #1 in a row for Mariah. Emotions is the title track to the 1991 release and I totally love how Mariah uses that high note all throughout the song!!Can't Let Go was the song that introduced me to Mariah. I had seen the music video on MTV and VH1 and ran out and got the tape of the 1991 release, Emotions, and I just love this beautiful ballad, it's one of my all time favorites from her!!Make It Happen, which is from Emotions from 1991, is a really cool upbeat song that I really love. I used to try to dance the way Mariah dances in the music video for this song which features a church. I love the music and the way Mariah sings so boldly at the end!I'll Be There is a cover of The Jackson 5 song which was recorded during a live performance called MTV Unplugged in 1992. I'll Be There became Mariah's 6th #1 and since I've heard both Mariah's and The Jackson 5's versions, I can honestly say that I love Mariah's more because of her voice, emotion, and soul!Dreamlover was the first single from Music Box that was released in 1993 and became Mariah's 7th #1! I love to sing and dance to this song every time I hear it!My all time favorite Mariah Carey song is Hero from the Music Box album which was released in 1993. It's gotten me through a lot of obstacles in my life with the message being so powerful! Hero became Mariah's 8th #1!The next song, Without You, is a Harry Nielson remake, from the 1993 release, Music Box. I've heard both versions and I must say that Mariah blows the original out of the water! Mariah's voice is incredible on this song and I love how she hits that really low register!Another favorite song of mine from the Music Box album, released in 1993, is Anytime You Need A Friend. I totally love this song and love how there is a choir singing in it, it's such an incredible song!! I love the club mixes of Anytime You Need A Friend Also! This song makes me feel like I'm in church and whenever I hear the part in the song that goes "If You Just Believe In Me, I Will Love You Endlessly", I think of Jesus because with the love of Jesus, you'll survive!!Another cover that blows the original out of the water is Endless Love!! It was originally by Diana Ross and Lionel Richie and after hearing both versions, it's obvious which version is better. Mariah and Luther Vandross sang this song together in 1994, with so much soul and emotion, and Mariah's vocals are incredible!!Fantasy, from Daydream that was released in 1995, was the first of many record-breaking triumphs for Mariah. Fantasy was Mariah's 9th #1 and it also was the first single to just debut at #1! I love the album version most because of the music which features a sample of the Tom Tom Club's Genius Of Love but I love all the versions.The 10th #1, One Sweet Day, from Daydream, released in 1995, set another record for Mariah, as it was the 2nd #1 to just debut at #1 on Billboard but it also spent 16 consecutive weeks at #1 and to this day, no one has ever broken that record! It's a very emotional ballad with Boyz II Men about losing a loved one, and I love it!!!Always Be My Baby, the 11th #1, became Mariah's 3rd #1 from Daydream, released in 1995. I just totally love this uptempo song so much and all the remixes and club mixes and always sing and dance whenever it comes on. The Always Club Mix is my all time favorite club mix from Mariah!!!Forever is yet another vocal masterpiece from Mariah's Daydream, released in 1995. Forever is actually one of the best romantic, vocal performances Mariah has ever done and it totally takes my breath away every time I hear it and it's one of my favorites from Mariah!!Another romantic ballad that makes me picture having a romantic evening under a sky full of stars is Underneath The Stars. Underneath The Stars, from Daydream, released in 1995, is a wonderful slow ballad!!Honey became Mariah's 12th #1 and it was the 3rd #1 to debut at the #1 spot on Billboard. Honey, which is the first single from Butterfly, released in 1997, started a more hip-hop and R&B; sound for Mariah. I love the Bad Boy Remix version of Honey best because it just sounds so cool but I love all versions of the song!!My all time favorite ballad from Butterfly, which was released in 1997, is the title track, Butterfly. I love Mariah's vocals and the way she sings on this beautiful slow ballad!!Mariah's 13th #1, from the 1997 release, Butterfly, is My All. I love this romantic ballad which includes this Spanish guitar. A wonderful, romantic slow ballad!!Sweetheart, from the 1998 release, #1's, is a cool R&B;/hip-hop song which features JD. It's a cool uptempo song and I love the part that goes "Won't You Be My Sweetheart, We Can Share A Story Book Romance."The next song features another favorite singer of mine, Whitney Houston, in When You Believe. This incredible duet is from the 1998 release, #1's and it's also from The Prince Of Egypt.I Still Believe is another cover of a ballad that Mariah remade from the original Brenda K. Starr version from the 80's. I love this Mariah version a little more because of Mariah's amazing voice. In the CD booklet from the 1998 release, #1's, it states that Mariah redid I Still Believe as a tribute to the one person who made Mariah's career happen, Brenda K. Starr!!Mariah's 14th #1 on Billboard is from her 1999 Rainbow album called Heartbreaker. Heartbreaker features Jay-Z and I love this cool uptempo R&B;/hip-hop song and all the remixes of it!!Thank God I Found You, which features Joe & 98 Degrees, from the 1999 Rainbow album, became Mariah's 15th #1 on Billboard. This is a really cool slow song and I like it a lot!!The best ballad from the Rainbow album, released in 1999, is Can't Take That Away (Mariah's Theme). I totally love this wonderful slow ballad and it's my favorite song off Rainbow. I love that part in the bridge that goes "Certainly The Lord Will Guide Me Where I Need To Go." I totally love it when she sings that part and I feel the same as Mariah, the Lord Jesus will guide ME where I need to go. Amazing!!!All I Want For Christmas Is You (So So Def Remix) is another 2000 Japanese bonus track, which features Jermaine Dupri & Lil Bow Wow. It's a R&B;/hip-hop remix of the original from 1994's Merry Christmas and it's pretty cool but I still love the original best!!This collection is a MUST HAVE for any Mariah Carey fan!! By the time Mariah releases another Greatest Hits, she'll have so many hits, it will take a 3 or 4 disc collection to be able to include all her hits!! DO NOT miss out on this magnificent collection from the greatest voice in the world, Mariah Carey!!!

Mariah and Luther Vandross sang this song together in 1994, with so much soul and emotion, and Mariah's vocals are incredible!!Fantasy, from Daydream that was released in 1995, was the first of many record-breaking triumphs for Mariah. I love the album version most because of the music which features a sample of the Tom Tom Club's Genius Of Love but I love all the versions.The 10th #1, One Sweet Day, from Daydream, released in 1995, set another record for Mariah, as it was the 2nd #1 to just debut at #1 on Billboard but it also spent 16 consecutive weeks at #1 and to this day, no one has ever broken that record! It's a very emotional ballad with Boyz II Men about losing a loved one, and I love it!!!Always Be My Baby, the 11th #1, became Mariah's 3rd #1 from Daydream, released in 1995. I just totally love this uptempo song so much and all the remixes and club mixes and always sing and dance whenever it comes on. The Always Club Mix is my all time favorite club mix from Mariah!!!Forever is yet another vocal masterpiece from Mariah's Daydream, released in 1995. Forever is actually one of the best romantic, vocal performances Mariah has ever done and it totally takes my breath away every time I hear it and it's one of my favorites from Mariah!!Another romantic ballad that makes me picture having a romantic evening under a sky full of stars is Underneath The Stars. Underneath The Stars, from Daydream, released in 1995, is a wonderful slow ballad!!Honey became Mariah's 12th #1 and it was the 3rd #1 to debut at the #1 spot on Billboard. I love Mariah's vocals and the way she sings on this beautiful slow ballad!!Mariah's 13th #1, from the 1997 release, Butterfly, is My All. I love this romantic ballad which includes this Spanish guitar. A wonderful, romantic slow ballad!!Sweetheart, from the 1998 release, #1's, is a cool R&B;/hip-hop song which features JD. Starr version from the 80's. I love this Mariah version a little more because of Mariah's amazing voice. Starr!!Mariah's 14th #1 on Billboard is from her 1999 Rainbow album called Heartbreaker. Heartbreaker features Jay-Z and I love this cool uptempo R&B;/hip-hop song and all the remixes of it!!Thank God I Found You, which features Joe & 98 Degrees, from the 1999 Rainbow album, became Mariah's 15th #1 on Billboard. This is a really cool slow song and I like it a lot!!The best ballad from the Rainbow album, released in 1999, is Can't Take That Away (Mariah's Theme). I totally love this wonderful slow ballad and it's my favorite song off Rainbow. I love that part in the bridge that goes "Certainly The Lord Will Guide Me Where I Need To Go." I totally love it when she sings that part and I feel the same as Mariah, the Lord Jesus will guide ME where I need to go. reviewText: Vulture Culture was released after Ammonia Avenue (my all-time favorite APP album) and not long before Stereotomy, so the Project was really churning out the music during this time.  While Ammonia Avenue is a masterpiece, the next two albums do not measure up to APP's high standards.  They are not bad albums.  APP just raised the bar with their earlier works.  Vulture Culture has an Indiana Jones look about it with the images of treasure seeking despite all dangers and, as the title track states, "never lend[ing] a loser a hand."  The songs, for the most part follow this theme.The first half of the album has the best of the material.  "Days are Numbers (The Traveller)" is one of APP's best tracks.  "Let's Talk About Me" is an excellent rocker with a lot of radio commentary in the background, including a reference to Wrigley Field, that makes the song different.  Eric Woolfson-sung tracks are almost always a sure bet as being the best material on the album; however, the ones on Vulture Culture are rather ordinary. "Sooner or Later," especially, is not up to Woolfson's standards. "Separate Lives" is my favorite of his primarily because of the cool synthesizers between the verses. "Same Old Sun" is a nice ballad but nothing approaching "Time" or "Eye in the Sky."  The second half is a little weaker.  The title track, for the most part, is unmemorable.  "Somebody Out There" is boring, devoid of any originality.  "Hawkeye" is a cool instrumental, though.  I can just see the snakes dancing along to it.  In sum, there is nothing really bad on Vulture Culture but, besides "Days Are Numbers," there's nothing spectacular either.

reviewText: First a Ginuwine album. Now a Lil' Kim joint. "What's wrong with you", you wonder. But again, this is yet another album I had to endure, ladies and lads. Kim Jones' third album, "La Bella Mafia", released after one of the worst mainstream rap albums I've ever heard(2000's "Notorious K.I.M."). Now, aside from her nasty Biggie-helmed '96 debut "Hard Core", I just don't like Kim's rapping...I just couldn't get into honey's post-Biggie agenda. She seemed(and still does seem) lost without Christopher Wallace's guidance. Although a sweet and caring person in real life, Kim seems like that sweet yet air headed aunt of yours. The nicest woman in the world but very confused. Yet, aside from my little experience in post-B.I.G. Kim fandom, I had to make this album for someone and I listened to it quite  a few times and will conclude that it's weak.Kim has nothing to say. It's the same, "I look so good", "My oral sex skills are this or that", "I'm balling", "Biggie this, Biggie that", and then to show her true confusion, she'll start talking about God or again, how she's gonna be okay without Big Poppa here. Kim's lyrics aren't that quotable and she doesn't seem believable. Being nasty and tired isn't representing Black women so she needs to get off that. Aside from boring topics, there's also a lack of confidence on Kim's part.  "La Bella Mafia" has too many guest stars who have NO chemistry with the 4'11" rapper. The tired sex rhyme, "Magic Stick", with flavor-of-the-month 50 Cent reeks of Sound Scan pandering. Yet the track is weak. The beat is listless. 50's verse is obviously phoned in and Kim's wicked sexual prowess sounds old and stale."Thug Luv" with Chi-Town legend Twista sounds so average and like with 50, Kim has no chemistry with the tied tongue wonder. The club romp "The Jump Off" is dated and a stereotypical Lil' Kim track. Timbaland lays down a surprisingly standard beat. "Hold It Now" and "This Is Who I Am" are boring and just some filler-ish tracks for Kim to brag about her fictional appeal."This Is A Warning" finds Kim threatening to "poision[an adversaries'] food" and singing to the R. Kelly slow jam "A Woman's Threat". The song is funny for all the wrong reasons. Aside from all the boring tricks and average production, surprisingly Kim, does have some halfway decent tricks in her Prada bag. "Can't F*** With Queen Bee" is humorous self-parody. Singing a haughty allegiance of self to the tune of Denience Williams' classic "Free". Along with Full Force singing background and Kim's quips, it's actually a good track. "Shake Ya Bum Bum" is a one-off club jam produced by Swizz Beats that's fun and harmless. Also, "Heavenly Father" finally finds Kim going beyond fashion, sex, and arrogance, to talk about her break from Junior M.A.F.I.A. and her deeply rooted faith. With a sped-up O'Jays sample, it's actually well-done and finds a new side to Kim.By the time this overfilled, overtly pointless set is over with "The Beehive", an eight minute rave up of her new crew of the same name (they're basically the new Junior M.A.F.I.A.) and the year old "Come Back For You" where she obligatory swings at rival/sister Foxy Brown as well as Eve and Trina(?),two other newbies who Kim feels are being disrespectful to the self-proclaimed "Queen Bee", you start yawning. Kim is a sweet person and outside of the nasty image, you feel the need to protect her. With  better producers, a more stable mental condition(this overbalance of Biggie is really unhealthy), and a more stable sound, I could see her succeeding. "La Bella Mafia" doesn't come close to Kim's ex-best friend Brown's stellar "Broken Silence" opus but since, the two one time multi-platinum dames seem to be plagued by bad decisions, industry drama, and personal turmoil(for Fox, it's the breakups, bad label deals, and a miscarriage; Kim, it's the bitter split with Puffy and Junior M.A.F.I.A. and the inability to fully move apart from Biggie, whose been dead for 6 years), maybe they could do a record together. Giving two embattled femme-cees who have the spunk a chance to grow, musically and importantly, as grown women.

reviewText: It took Browne over 10 years to put out an album of new material following "Looking East" in 1996.  "Naked" is a decent enough comeback although not as good as much of his earlier material.  The album begins with the title track which to me sounds like he is trying to recapture some of his romantic storytelling of yesteryear, but does not quite pull it off.  In fact I feel the same way about much of this album.  The material is good, but just not on the same level of similar things he has done previously.  There are a few highlights.  The politically charged "Casino Nation" finds Browne in fine topical form.  "Walking Town" is a duet with Don Henley which is good.  "Sergio Leone" is another cool song that meanders for almost 8 minutes before abruptly ending.  I have seen other reviews that criticize this song for never really going anywhere and I would tend to agree.  The writing style reminds me a lot of Warren Zevon, but although I think the meat of the song is great, it never really concludes which is a determent.  This album is ok, but considering it took 12 years to come out, it probably could have been better.

reviewText: I just finished listening to this old vinyl record for the upteenth time.I never tire of it and from glancing at the reviews many others feel the same.It's hard to believe this was recorded over 40 years ago in 1968.My album is an original recording and it is so good to hear the voices of Johnny and June in those earlier days.The discussions between Cash and his audience of prisoners result in a haunting memory of what it was to actually go into a prison and play and record their music and the reaction of the prisoners.If one were to try to come up with the top 10 Country Music albums of all time;it would almost be a certainty that this one be included.Rather than the typical "liner notes" found on the back of an album cover;there is an extensive hand printed message by Johnny wherein he talks about the whole world of prison and prisoners and what he makes of it.After reading these notes,the reader is left with the impression that Cash put his heart and soul into his music and believed what he was singing about.His music was truly a message and not just something he did for a living or the money and fame.That is why he had such a large following and why his music has lived so long and why we will continue to listen to it for a long time.That is why he deserves the title "A Legend".
summary: "The culture of a thousand years is shattered with the clanging of the cell door behind you." Johnny Cash
